title: viscum album subsp. meridianum
intro: Viscum album subsp. meridianum, commonly known as European mistletoe, is a parasitic plant that grows on the branches of various deciduous trees, such as oak, ash, and elm. It has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including its ability to stimulate the immune system, reduce inflammation, and alleviate symptoms of cancer, such as pain and fatigue. The therapeutic actions of European mistletoe are thought to be due to its bioactive constituents, which include viscoside, lectins, and polyphenolic compounds, that have anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory effects. The plant's bioactive constituents may also contribute to its ability to inhibit the growth of cancer cells and induce apoptosis, or programmed cell death, in cancer cells.
